facts.value: The 2026/27 Research Regulations cover PhD (including an intercalated MBBS PhD), MD(Res), and MPhil. MPhil is FHEQ level 7; PhD and MD(Res) are level 8. The regulations exclude MRes/taught integrated years and EngD, which has separate regulations. Study is conducted in English. MPhil may be a directly registered award or a transfer/exit outcome; it should not be presented as an independent taught course.

facts.value: Normal PhD/MPhil entry includes a UK upper-second honours degree plus a Master’s; an upper-second MSci/MEng; an appropriate registrable medical qualification or Master’s at FHEQ level 7; or an approved professional written-examination qualification. Recognised overseas equivalents and English requirements apply. Individual courses may set higher requirements. Lower qualifications require an approved department exception; do not treat generic equivalency as automatic entry.

Full registration itself is not required when the applicant is eligible for it. The Director of Postgraduate Studies may allow registration without this GMC condition if the research has no patient contact. A later loss of eligibility or registration can trigger a review of continuation.

facts.value: PhD/MD(Res) require research, thesis/viva, departmental training, and at least four ECRI skills credits: two by ESA and two more by LSR. They also require plagiarism training and, for entrants from 1 September 2026, Trusted Research e-learning. DACR diagnostic training applies to registrations from 1 September 2025 and is due by ESA. Milestones: ESA by 12 months full-time/24 part-time; LSR by 24/48; progress review by 36/72. A failed progress review may lead to withdrawal or transfer from PhD to MPhil. MPhil requires at least two skills credits and plagiarism training before examination, plus departmental reviews. These are completion/progression requirements, not entry tests. If an academic assessment is passed but skills, plagiarism, or DACR training is incomplete, conditional progression may be allowed subject to a completion deadline agreed with the department, ECRI, or Academic English; missing training does not automatically mean failure. Normal thesis-submission limits: PhD/MD(Res) within 48 months full-time/96 part-time; MPhil within 24/48; internal MBBS intercalated PhD normally within 36/72. Examination-entry forms are due at 44/88 months for PhD/MD(Res) and 20/40 for MPhil. UKRI CDT/DFA handbooks may set their own milestone/submission deadlines. Approved extensions can alter dates. These limits are completion limits, not advertised course durations.

facts.value: Most research is normally at Imperial. Approved external research requires minimum university attendance of12 months for PhD/MD(Res) or six months for MPhil. Split PhD requires12 months of active Imperial attendance, excluding interruption/writing-up; PRI requires two months each academic year, excluding writing-up. Advanced-standing active study is at least12 full-time or24 part-time months. Writing-up needs approval, normally after36 full-time or72 part-time months, with earlier entry possible after24/48 months except approved advanced-standing/transfer cases. Writing-up normally lasts up to12 full-time or24 part-time months. These research-location/registration conditions do not create automatic remote study.

facts.value: Relevant engineering, physical science, mathematics, biomedical/physiology/medical backgrounds; first/good upper-second subject to central qualifications. Contact supervisor; two academic references from institutional email; full transcripts; CV up to two pages and personal statement/research proposal up to two pages. Advertised studentships do not require a proposal. Interview in English normally 30–40 minutes with two staff, in person/telephone/video. Applications all year; funding often early November/January (yearless guidance). Decisions typically 8–10 weeks after complete submission; acceptance is not funding.

facts.value: Entry: first-class undergraduate degree, upper-second integrated Master’s, or upper-second Bachelor’s plus standalone Master’s; discuss special cases with admissions. Research backgrounds include engineering, physical, mathematical, biological, and medical sciences. PhD duration is four years full-time. Intake dates are the first working Monday of October, January, April, and July. Two academic referees are required, excluding the proposed supervisor; complete documents are needed before a decision. The online English interview is at least 30 minutes with two staff. Normal processing takes 10–12 weeks. The two-page statement plus research proposal is specifically scholarship documentation, not stated as a universal admission requirement. Published scholarship rounds—3 November 2025, 12 January 2026, and 2 March 2026, all at 23:59 UK time—apply to 2026/27 and must not be silently carried into 2027.

facts.value: The general Computing PhD target is normally a first-class or distinction Master’s in a relevant scientific/technical subject; an undergraduate degree is normally equivalent to UK 2:1. Bachelor-only applicants are normally not considered, but outstanding applicants or those with extensive relevant industry/research experience may formally apply with evidence of compensating factors; the department will not pre-assess exceptions by email. Standard English is required. Submit a CV with linked publications, all Bachelor’s/Master’s transcripts, two references, a 1–2-page personal statement, and an original 3–4-page research statement with literature references. The statements must be written by the applicant without generative AI. Suggest 3–4 supervisors. Normal review starts only after a formal application. An interview may ask the applicant to present a past project or discuss assigned papers. This general target differs from the AI4Health target. For April/October 2027 entry, rounds open 1 October 2026, 1 December 2026, 1 February 2027, and 1 April 2027; decisions are due 15 February, 15 April, 15 June, and 15 July 2027 respectively. The source does not publish an exact deadline time.

facts.value: Entry: UK MEng in electrical engineering or related subject at 2:1/first, or BEng at 2:1/first plus Master’s at Merit or higher. International applicants normally need the equivalent of a UK 2:1 Bachelor’s and Master’s at Merit. Higher English is required. Contact a supervisor; submit CV 1–2 pages, personal statement 1–2 pages, research statement 2–3 pages, and two references. Applications are normally reviewed after both references arrive. Shortlisted applicants interview on Teams with the proposed supervisor and a colleague. Decisions typically take eight weeks. Intakes are October, early January, 1 April, and 1 July. Applications are accepted year-round, subject to funding deadlines.

Provide two references, excluding the proposed supervisor, using a professional email or accepted signed headed-PDF alternative. Complete the independent interview and NHLI01/department approval. Document secured funding or a funding plan/scholarship; studentship selection precedes the formal application. A research proposal may be completed within six weeks after the start, unlike Computing’s requirement to submit a proposal with the application. Employment alone is not degree admission. For the Imperial staff scheme, the contract must cover the degree; honorary and directly externally funded staff are ineligible. NHS staff discounts are separate. Apply 2–3 months ahead; backdating is not permitted.

Agree a supervisor and complete the departmental interview before applying through My Imperial. The department advertises PhD/MPhil routes lasting 4 years full-time or 8 years part-time. Minimum research registration is 24 months full-time or 48 months part-time; generic PhD duration of 3–4 years full-time or 5–6 part-time is not imposed. Six research areas are within the departmental degree, not separate admissions programmes. Applications are accepted year-round, with most starts in September/October. Admission is not a scholarship application; check funding separately.
